admission.contract: A job-file option line is admitted by `__parse_jobs_ini` into the section option vector and then passed unchanged into `fio_options_parse`.
admission.predicate: store.hit && parse.hit && parse.time > store.time && store.opts_vec == parse.opts_vec && store.num_opts == parse.num_opts && store.last_opt == parse.last_opt
limitations: This binds admission of a parsed option line to `fio_options_parse`, but it does not by itself prove the option text contains `$ncpus`.
The exact public example string is only tied in combination with the later keyword-match event in `fio_keyword_replace`.

root.contract: `fio_keyword_replace` reaches a state where the matched keyword starts later than the beginning of the option string and the subsequent copy length is derived from the advanced `opt` pointer instead of the remaining suffix length.
root.predicate: copy_state.hit && copy_state.olen > 0 && copy_state.tail_len > 0 && copy_state.copy_len == copy_state.olen + copy_state.kw_len - 1 && copy_state.copy_len > copy_state.tail_len + 1
limitations: This contract requires a nonempty suffix after the keyword because the buggy `memcpy` is guarded by `if (strlen(opt))`.

The public issue names `description=$ncpus`, but in this source that exact terminal-keyword shape would skip the `memcpy`; the issue text and code therefore do not give an unambiguous executable binding for that exact example.

target.contract: The same miscomputed length is consumed by the `memcpy` in `fio_keyword_replace`, making the keyword-substitution copy extend past the available suffix bytes and/or past the replacement buffer capacity.
target.predicate: memcpy_use.hit && memcpy_use.copy_len == root.copy_state.copy_len && memcpy_use.tail_len == root.copy_state.tail_len && (memcpy_use.copy_len > memcpy_use.tail_len + 1 || memcpy_use.dst_off + memcpy_use.copy_len > memcpy_use.dst_cap)
limitations: This binds the dangerous operation to the same state as `root`, but it does not identify whether the observed overflow manifests as a source over-read, a destination over-write, or both in a particular run.
Because the public issue’s concrete example appears inconsistent with the `strlen(opt)` guard in this vulnerable source, the exact crashing input shape remains ambiguous from source plus issue alone.
